subject.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model

question: Should `agents.defaults.subagents.model` override a named agent’s primary model across all native subagent and isolated-cron paths?
rationale: Both opposite precedence contracts have been merged into shipped code, and choosing either changes existing users’ provider/model routing; implementation review cannot safely infer the intended compatibility policy.

options.title: Global default wins everywhere
options.body: Merge this narrow shared-selector alignment while retaining per-agent `subagents.model` as the only higher-priority configured override.

options.title: Named agent primary wins
options.body: Reject this PR and revise the spawn planner and documentation to restore agent-primary-first behavior consistently.

options.title: Split main and named semantics
options.body: Pause both overlapping PRs and define distinct precedence for the default agent and named agents before implementation.

recommendation.title: Global default wins everywhere
recommendation.body: Merge this narrow shared-selector alignment while retaining per-agent `subagents.model` as the only higher-priority configured override.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the central shared cron/fallback refactor and has already reviewed the exact contract conflict across the affected paths.
